subject.title: feat(setup): offer native Windows and WSL gateway modes

question: Should the uncontained native Windows gateway be offered to all onboarding users as an explicit lower-isolation choice, or gated as experimental until containment and installer-trust policies mature?
rationale: Tests can verify ownership and lifecycle mechanics, but they cannot decide the acceptable product security boundary for executing the gateway and a live installer directly in the Windows user context.

options.title: Gate Native Initially
options.body: Keep WSL as the normal onboarding path and place native mode behind an explicit experimental opt-in while collecting containment and operational evidence.

options.title: Offer Native Broadly
options.body: Retain the visible native choice with strong lower-isolation disclosure and explicitly accept the Windows user-context and mutable-installer trust model.

options.title: Defer Native Mode
options.body: Pause the native onboarding surface until the related containment work and a verified installer distribution model are available.

recommendation.title: Gate Native Initially
recommendation.body: Keep WSL as the normal onboarding path and place native mode behind an explicit experimental opt-in while collecting containment and operational evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the most detailed security/parity review and implemented the branch's current lifecycle and WSL-first framing changes.
